problem: Agree with the writer's doubt: ਤਿਤੁ ਘਰਿ ਜਾਇ ਬਸੈ ਅਬਿਨਾਸੀ has ਅਬਿਨਾਸੀ as the subject of ਬਸੈ (the Imperishable comes to dwell in that heart). Our Hindi makes the devotee go and live where the Imperishable is, which needs an added relative clause the verse does not have. Hindi corrected to match the English.
fix: हरिके नामसे मनको जगाओ; दसों दिशाओंमें दौड़ता हुआ (मन) ठिकाने आ जाता है। जिसके हृदयमें वह हरि बसता है, उसे कोई विघ्न नहीं लगता। कलियुग तपता हुआ है, हरिका नाम शीतल है। (उसका) स्मरण कर-करके सदा सुख पाओ। भय मिट जाता है, आशा पूरी होती है; भक्ति-भावसे आत्मामें प्रकाश होता है। उस (हृदयरूपी) घरमें अविनाशी (प्रभु) आ बसता है। नानक कहता है, (उसकी) यमकी फाँसी कट गयी।

problem: Agree with the writer, on balance: line 1 has no relative ਜੋ…ਸੋ (unlike line 2, ਜਨਮਿ ਮਰੈ ਸੋ…), so it reads most simply as object–verb–subject: the true servant (ਜਨੁ ਸਾਚਾ) speaks (ਕਹੈ) this essential reflection (ਤਤੁ ਬੀਚਾਰੁ), and line 2 is what he says. Our Hindi (one who speaks it is true) is a known reading, but the Hindi and English should agree; owner to confirm. Hindi in line with the English:
fix: सच्चा जन यह तत्त्वका विचार कहता है — जो जन्मता-मरता रहता है, वह कच्चा-ही-कच्चा है। प्रभुकी सेवासे आवागमन मिटता है; अपनापन छोड़कर गुरुदेवकी शरणमें जाओ। इस प्रकार रत्न-जैसे (मनुष्य-) जन्मका उद्धार होता है। प्राणोंके आधार हरिका स्मरण करो। अनेक उपायोंसे, स्मृतियों, शास्त्रों और वेदोंका विचार करनेसे भी (जीव) नहीं छूटता। मन लगाकर हरिकी भक्ति करो। हे नानक! (इससे) मनचाहा फल मिलता है।

problem: ਜਨੁ is rendered 'devotee' here but 'servant' everywhere else in the batch and in the writer's own refrains (ਜਨੁ / ਸੇਵਕੁ / ਦਾਸ: servant).
fix: The true servant states this essential truth: whoever keeps being born and dying is unripe, utterly unripe. Coming and going in birth and death ends by serving God: give up self-conceit and take refuge with the divine Guru. In this way the jewel of human birth is redeemed; remember the Lord, Har Har, the mainstay of life. No one is released by countless efforts, nor by pondering the Simritis, Shastras and Vedas. Worship the Lord with your mind fixed on him. Nanak, you will receive the fruit your heart desires.

problem: 'The illness does not go with countless remedies' is not natural English ('go' alone); 'go away'.
fix: The wealth for which you rise and run to the four corners of the earth, that wealth you will find by serving the Lord. The peace you long for every day, my friend, that peace lies in love for the company of the holy. The honour for which you do good deeds, for that honour, hurry to the Lord's refuge. The illness does not go away with countless remedies; the illness is cured when the medicine of the Lord is applied. Of all treasures, the treasure is the Lord's Name. Repeat it, Nanak, and be accepted in the Lord's Court.

problem: Dangling participle: 'Worshipping the One, sins have gone' makes the sins the worshippers.
fix: Repeat the One alone, praise the One alone. Remember the One, and long, my mind, for the One alone. Sing the endless praises of the One. With mind and body repeat the one Lord's Name. The Lord himself is the One, the One alone. God is fully pervading, filling all. The countless expanses of creation came from the One. Through worship of the One, sins have gone. Mind and body are dyed deep within in the colour of the one God. By the Guru's grace, Nanak, the One has been known.

problem: 'Your servant ... begs God for a gift: in your grace, Lord, grant me your Name' mixes address and third person in one sentence (whose servant?). ਪ੍ਰਭ is naturally the vocative here, as the rest of the pauri addresses God.
fix: Ashtapadi. Your servant, a beggar, begs you, God, for a gift: in your grace, Lord, grant me your Name. I beg for the dust of the holy ones' feet. Supreme Lord, fulfil my longing: may I sing God's praises for ever and ever; with every breath, God, may I meditate on you. May love for your lotus feet take hold of me; may I worship God with devotion day after day. You alone are my shelter and my support. Nanak asks for God's Name, the most excellent of all.

problem: 'he sees the Lord pervading all' adds 'he sees': ਰਵਿ ਰਹਿਆ ਸਦ ਸੰਗਿ ਹਜੂਰੀ says only that the Lord pervades and is ever with him, present (our Hindi likewise).
fix: The servant's wish has been fulfilled; from the True Guru he has received pure understanding. God has become merciful to his servant and has made him joyful for ever. His bonds are cut and the servant is free; the pain of birth and death and all doubt are gone. His desire is met, his longing wholly fulfilled; the Lord pervades all, ever with him, ever present. He to whom he belonged has united him with himself. Nanak, through devotion he merges in the Naam.

problem: ਜਿ ਕੀਆ ਜਾਨੈ is the one who knows (acknowledges) what one has done; 'what is done for him' adds 'for him' and narrows it to deeds done for God. Fix also includes the womb gloss proposed in the doubt line below.
fix: How can he be forgotten, who does not let our toil go to waste? How can he be forgotten, who recognises what we have done? How can he be forgotten, who has given us everything? How can he be forgotten, who is the life of all beings? How can he be forgotten, who keeps us safe in the fire (of the womb)? By the Guru's grace only a rare one perceives this. How can he be forgotten, who draws us out of poison, and joins again those parted from him for lifetimes? The perfect Guru has made this essential truth clear. Nanak, his servants have meditated on their God.

problem: Writer's doubt (fire of the womb not added). Agree that the words say only ਅਗਨਿ, but disagree with leaving bare 'the fire': most readers will not know which fire is meant, style §2 allows a one-off round-bracket gloss exactly for this, our Hindi already has (गर्भकी), and the work itself says ਗਰਭ ਅਗਨਿ in a04.p1 (rendered 'the fire of the womb' in batch 01). Recommend the gloss (fix includes the addition fix above).
fix: How can he be forgotten, who does not let our toil go to waste? How can he be forgotten, who recognises what we have done? How can he be forgotten, who has given us everything? How can he be forgotten, who is the life of all beings? How can he be forgotten, who keeps us safe in the fire (of the womb)? By the Guru's grace only a rare one perceives this. How can he be forgotten, who draws us out of poison, and joins again those parted from him for lifetimes? The perfect Guru has made this essential truth clear. Nanak, his servants have meditated on their God.

problem: 'behold his sight' reads as his eyesight; batches 01–03 use 'the sight of him / of God' for ਦਰਸਨੁ/ਦਰਸੁ.
fix: Love has welled up in me, the sweetness of love, and longing; within mind and body this alone is my aim: to behold the sight of him with my eyes and be at peace. The mind blossoms as it washes the feet of the holy. The devotees are dyed in his love, mind and body; only a rare one gains their company. Be merciful and give me one thing: that by the Guru's grace I may repeat the Naam. His praise cannot be told. Nanak, he is present in all.

problem: A doubt the writer did not record: ਗੁਰ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਦਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਿ ਲਇਆ is past (ਲਇਆ, word sheet: took, obtained), but the meaning turns it into a wish ('that I may repeat'), which also decides whose praise ਤਾ ਕੀ ਉਪਮਾ is. Our Hindi and Khalsa read it as the writer does, so the meaning can stay; record it for the owner.
fix: {"id": "a20.p6", "issue": "ਗੁਰ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਦਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਿ ਲਇਆ ॥ ਤਾ ਕੀ ਉਪਮਾ ਕਹੀ ਨ ਜਾਇ: ਲਇਆ is past; the meaning takes the line as the content of the prayer (that I may repeat the Naam) and ਤਾ ਕੀ as God's.", "our reading": "Be merciful and give me one thing: that by the Guru's grace I may repeat the Naam. His (God's) praise cannot be told (with our Hindi and Khalsa).", "alternatives": "One who by the Guru's grace has repeated the Naam, his glory cannot be told; Nanak, (God) pervades all."}

problem: 'When the Master was stainless, beyond the senses and unfathomable' implies he is not so now. ਜਬ ਨਾਥ ਨਿਰੰਜਨ ਅਗੋਚਰ ਅਗਾਧੇ is 'when there was only the Master, stainless…' (as in the parallel lines and our Hindi: …नाथ ही था). Fix also includes the style point below.
fix: When the Imperishable was seated at ease in his own place, then tell me, where were birth, death and destruction? When there was only that perfect Creator God, then tell me, who could feel the terror of death's messenger? When God, unmanifest and beyond the senses, was the One alone, then of whom could Chitra and Gupta, the recorders of deeds, ask an account? When there was only the Master, stainless, beyond the senses and unfathomable, then who was set free, and who was tied in bonds? He himself, by himself, is the wonder. Nanak, he himself brought forth his own form.

problem: ਜਮ ਕੀ ਤ੍ਰਾਸ rendered 'the terror of death'; the writer's refrains give ਜਮ as death's messenger (as in a24.p7). Fix also includes the error fix above.
fix: When the Imperishable was seated at ease in his own place, then tell me, where were birth, death and destruction? When there was only that perfect Creator God, then tell me, who could feel the terror of death's messenger? When God, unmanifest and beyond the senses, was the One alone, then of whom could Chitra and Gupta, the recorders of deeds, ask an account? When there was only the Master, stainless, beyond the senses and unfathomable, then who was set free, and who was tied in bonds? He himself, by himself, is the wonder. Nanak, he himself brought forth his own form.

problem: Ungrammatical: 'The one whom God himself gives understanding' needs 'to whom'.
fix: Ashtapadi. He himself speaks, and he himself is the one who listens. He himself is the One, and he himself the vast expanse. When it pleases him, he brings forth the creation; by his own will he draws it back into himself. Nothing is apart from you; on your own thread you have strung the whole world. The one to whom God himself gives understanding, that servant receives the true Name. He looks on all alike and knows the essence of reality. Nanak, he is the conqueror of the whole world.

problem: Dangling participle: 'Repeating the Name of the Fearless One, all fear is erased' makes fear the one who repeats.
fix: Where can anyone go far from him? One is saved by meditating on the Protector. When one repeats the Name of the Fearless One, all fear is erased; by God's grace a mortal is set free. One whom God protects has no pain; repeating the Naam, the mind finds peace. Anxiety goes and pride is erased; no one can equal that servant. The valiant Guru stands over his head. Nanak, his tasks are all fulfilled.

problem: 'seeing his sight' reads as his eyesight; use 'the sight of him' (as in batches 01–03).
fix: Perfect is the wisdom of him whose glance is nectar; seeing the sight of him, the world is saved. Matchless are his lotus feet; fruitful is the sight of the Lord, and beautiful his form. Blessed is his service, and his servant is accepted; he is the knower of hearts, the Supreme Being. One in whose mind he dwells is filled with joy; death does not come near him. They have become immortal and attained the immortal state, Nanak, who meditated on the Lord in the Saadh Sangat.

problem: Ungrammatical/wrong sense: 'He alone has seen it whom God himself has shown' says God showed that person; needs 'to whom God himself has shown it'.
fix: Ashtapadi. In the company of the saints I have seen God within; God's Name has become sweet to me. All things are within the heart of the One, though they appear in many colours and kinds. God's Name is the nectar, the nine treasures; its resting place is within the body. There is the trance of the void, and there the unstruck melody sounds, the divine music that no instrument makes; its wonder and amazement cannot be told. He alone has seen it to whom God himself has shown it. Nanak, that servant gains understanding.

problem: 'seeing his sight' reads as his eyesight; 'the sight of him' keeps the writer's open reading (saint or God) of the doubt, which I agree with.
fix: To the saints all they behold is God; in the hearts of the saints is all righteousness. The saints hear words of good; they are merged in the Lord who pervades all. Such is the conduct of one who has known him: all that the holy one says is true. Whatever happens, he accepts it gladly; he knows God as the doer and the cause of all doing. For him God dwells within, and outside too it is he alone. Nanak, seeing the sight of him, all are enchanted.

problem: Optional, for agreement with the English (writer listed our Hindi as an alternative, not as wrong): ਅੰਤਰਗਤਿ means being within (word sheet: भीतर (हृदयमें) व्याप्त; Skt. antargata, gone within), not अन्तर्यामी. Agree with the writer's English reading.
fix: वह आप सत्य है, उसका किया सब सत्य है; उस प्रभुसे ही सारी उत्पत्ति है। जब उसे भाता है, तब (सृष्टिका) विस्तार करता है; जब उसे भाता है, तब (फिर) एकंकार (अकेला) हो जाता है। उसकी अनेक शक्तियाँ देखी-समझी नहीं जा सकतीं; जिसे वह चाहता है, उसे (अपनेमें) मिला लेता है। किसे निकट और किसे दूर कहा जाय? वह आप ही आप सब ओर भरपूर है। जिसे वह स्वयं जना देता है कि वह भीतर (हृदयमें) बसा है, हे नानक! उस जनको वह आप (अपनी) समझ देता है।

problem: Gopal is glossed in a20.p7 (and a15.p1) but not in this ashtapadi, and Damodar is never glossed; most readers will not know either name.
fix: For well-being, happiness, poise and bliss, worship the Lord of supreme bliss in the Saadh Sangat. Ward off hell and save your soul; drink the nectar of Gobind's praises. In your heart dwell on the one all-pervading Lord, whose form is one and whose colours are many. He is Gopal, sustainer of the world, Damodar (a name of the Lord), merciful to the meek, destroyer of pain, wholly kind. Remember, remember the Naam, God's Name, again and again. Nanak, this alone is the support of the soul.

problem: Ambiguous: in '…the wealth of the Lord, Nanak, who is granted it' the relative clause attaches to Nanak (or the Lord). The verse means only the one to whom it is granted departs with this wealth.
fix: Saints, friends, sing the praise of God, with a mind alert and fixed on him alone. The Sukhmani, the jewel of peace, is poise, Gobind's praises and the Naam; one in whose mind it dwells becomes a treasure-house. All his desires are fulfilled; he becomes the foremost of men, renowned in all the world. He reaches the highest place of all, and comes and goes no more. Nanak, that servant alone departs having earned the wealth of the Lord: the one to whom it is granted.

problem: ਦੁਲਭ ਦੇਹ is the body hard to obtain (word sheet; MW durlabha: hard to be obtained, rare), not 'precious', and 'human' is added; the writer renders the same phrase 'this body so hard to obtain' in a22.p5, as batch 01 does in a06.p3.
fix: One in whose mind it dwells, who listens to it with love, that servant remembers the Lord God. His pain of birth and death is taken away; this body, so hard to obtain, is redeemed at once. Spotless is his glory, and his speech is nectar; the one Name fills his mind. Pain, sickness, fear and doubt are gone; he is called holy, and his deeds are spotless. His glory rises above all. It is for these virtues, Nanak, that its name is Sukhmani, the jewel of peace.
